title: HR and Payroll Officer
company: Not For Profit People - Agency - Permanent
description:
HR and Payroll Officer

Are you an organised and people-focused HR professional with payroll experience who enjoys delivering excellent service and building strong working relationships?

We are seeking an enthusiastic HR and Payroll Officer to join the Human Resources team in this full-time, permanent role.

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full employee lifecycle while building expertise in both HR and payroll. It is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing attention to detail with relationship-building and who takes pride in delivering a high-quality service.

Position: HR & Payroll Officer

Location: Kidlington, Oxford/hybrid

Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Salary: £37,751.95 - £40,655.94 per annum

Contract: Permanent

Closing Date: Midnight on Tuesday 18 November 2026. Interviews will take place at Church House, Oxford: Friday 27 November 2026

The Role

You will join the Human Resources team, playing a key role in supporting employees, clergy, managers and senior leaders across the Diocese. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to meaningful work, ensuring people are supported through efficient payroll, recruitment, learning and development, and employee lifecycle processes.

This is a varied and rewarding role within a professional and collaborative HR team that supports both the Diocesan Board of Finance and Diocesan Board of Education. You will provide reliable, confidential and people-centred HR and payroll support that helps employees, clergy and leaders do their best work.

You will also play a key role in delivering recruitment and onboarding activities, be the first point of contact for payroll-related matters and will help maintain robust controls and ensure compliance with statutory and organisational requirements.

About You

We are looking for an experienced HR and payroll professional who is highly organised, accurate and customer-focused, with a passion for providing excellent support and advice. You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, handling sensitive information with discretion and working collaboratively with a wide range of stakeholders.

You will bring experience of HR administration and payroll processing within a busy organisational environment, together with strong communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

You will also have:
- Sound knowledge of generalist HR practices and payroll administration.
- Up-to-date knowledge of UK employment legislation and HMRC requirements relating to payroll, tax and statutory payments.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, learning and development, employee relations and performance management activities.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, and experience using HR management systems and payroll systems.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail, particularly when working with payroll and employee data and maintaining accurate employee records.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

A CIPD and/or CIPP qualification or membership would be advantageous, although applications are welcomed from candidates with transferable skills and experience.

You do not need to be a practising Christian to work here. Around half of staff are not practising Christians, but all are comfortable working within the Christian ethos and values that underpin the organisation's work.

The successful candidate must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews. We are particularly keen to receive applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority heritage and disabled candidates, who are currently underrepresented.

You may have experience in other areas such as HR, Human Resources, Personnel, People, HR Officer, Human Resources Officer, Personnel Officer, People Officer, Payroll, Payroll Officer, Payroll Assistant, HR Assistant, Finance Officer, Finance Assistant, HR and Finance, HR and Payroll.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People.

title: Finance and Resources Administrator
description:
Finance and Resources Administrator

Do you have excellent customer facing, administrative and communication skills? Enjoy working with a wide variety of people?

Permanent, Fulltime, 35 hours per week

Office Based, 5 days a week at CMS House, Oxford.

Starting salary £28,170 per annum, with a generous pension contribution: up to 10 per cent employer contribution on annual salary

CMS offers 36 days of annual leave pro rata (including bank holidays) as well as enhanced paid sickness, maternity, paternity and adoption leave.

CMS supports the mental wellbeing of its employees and offers a generous rewards and wellbeing package, including:

o access to 24/7 employee assistance programme with qualified counsellors

o regular wellbeing coffee mornings

o support on menopause for women

o up to three volunteer days a year

o up to three family emergency leave days a year

o retreats and resources for prayer life

We welcome applications from everyone. We particularly welcome applications from women and individuals from minority groups as they are currently underrepresented within our organisation at this level. All appointments are made on merit of skill, experience and potential as set out in the job description and person specification.

Your role

We are looking for a proactive team player who enjoys a varied role combining reception (front of house), administrator and cross-team support. You will provide a warm reception to visitors, manage meeting logistics and provide administrative coordination.

The organisation you'll be joining

Church Mission Society is comprised of people who are passionate about mission and fired up about helping people follow Jesus. For over 200 years CMS has been at the forefront of global mission, living out the gospel of Jesus, seeing lives changed and communities transformed. If you join CMS you will find an organisation that has been reinvigorated with a fresh vision to make disciples of Jesus among people at the edges, both in the UK and around the world.

What you'll need to succeed

The successful candidate will be educated to A level standard or equivalent, with proven administrative experience in a busy team environment, customer service or facilities experience, strong written and verbal communication skills, and excellent organisational skills.

You will also need to be in sympathy with the aims and values of Church Mission Society.

Further details can be found in the job description and person specification, available to download from the CMS website.

Our commitment to you

Our core values of being pioneering, relational, faithful and evangelistic are integral to everything we do, and we work hard to ensure that every member of staff is valued, supported and encouraged to continually learn and develop their skills.

We are committed to the safeguarding and protection of the people we serve, our partners, our volunteers, and our staff. We believe that every child or adult we come into contact with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm and abuse. Our recruitment and selection processes are in line with our Safeguarding Policy and the SCHR Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, which CMS is a member of as part of our commitment to safeguarding.

Closing date

We must get your application by midnight on Sunday 15th November.

Interviews are planned to be held on Thursday 26th November at CMS House, Oxford.

To apply

Please send your application form and CV via or website or by post to HR Team, Church Mission Society, Watlington Road, Oxford OX4 6 BZ. CVs will only be considered when sent with a completed application form, which is available to download from our website.

Candidates for all UK roles must already be eligible to work in the UK, with a valid visa and work permit if required.

As a member of the Inter-agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, CMS has committed to systematically check with previous employers from the last five years for any 'SEAH' (Sexual Exploitation, Abuse or Harassment) issues relating to all potential new hires.
